messages:
Alex: Quick follow-up from yesterday's RFC meeting — I want to propose we land on a 'policy microcontracts' model for the routing engine. Basic idea: split matcher (compatibility) out from scoring (weights/penalties) and version each independently. Keeps fast path tiny and lets scoring evolve without invalidating matchers.

Priya: Microcontracts = small stable API between matchers and scorers? can you sketch the contract shape?

Alex: Exactly. Contract is just the set of signals matchers guarantee (region, tier, hard-capacity, model_family, latency_bucket) + optional hints. Scorers consume those signals and compute a score. Matchers must be deterministic and cheap. Scorers can be heavier and have versioned fallback.

Lina: How do we enforce determinism for matchers? We already have nasty edge cases with topology updates.

Chris: Perf concern — if we decouple, will we double-hop lookups? matchers -> scoring -> route resolution? We need to avoid extra RPCs on hot path.

Alex: Good call. Implementation plan: both matchers and scorers live in same process for hot path, but are logically versioned. The runtime loads matcher vN and scorer vM together into a policy bundle. The 'contract' is checked at bundle load time. No extra RPC per request.

Mateo: What about cache semantics? If scorer changes but matcher stays same, we can reuse route compatibility cache; only score cache invalidates. Conversely, matcher change requires compatibility cache invalidation. We should surface separate cache keys: `compat_v{n}` and `score_v{m}`.

Priya: This aligns with our earlier TTL debate. Suggest cache key schema: `tenant:route:compat_v{n}:input_hash` and `tenant:route:score_v{m}:compat_key`. That way we avoid recomputing the matcher for the same input if compat_v unchanged.

Lina: What about tenant overrides and emergency blackout rules? If tenant overrides add extra matchers, we need precedence semantics.

Alex: Proposal: matcher precedence stack: global < org < tenant. When resolving bundle we flatten the stack into a single effective matcher with a resulting contract version hash. Tenant overrides change the compat hash and thus invalidate compat cache — expected.

Chris: Scoring penalties — we've been using monolithic penalty buckets which are hard to tune. Can we split penalties into orthogonal axes (latency_penalty, cost_penalty, region_preference) and have a small DSL to compose them?

Alex: Yes — split penalties and make them composable. Example snippet of scoring config:```
scorer_version: "v3"
penalties: [
  {type: "latency", func: "exp", scale: 0.001},
  {type: "cost", func: "linear", slope: 0.5},
  {type: "region_pref", weights: {us: 0, eu: 0.2, apac: 0.5}}
]
fallbacks: [ {when: "score_unavailable", to: "scorer:v2"} ]
```

Mateo: Observability? Need per-penalty buckets in metrics and traces so we can attribute why a route lost. Also want an explain endpoint returning the breakdown.

Priya: +1. Add a `score_breakdown` field to the route decision proto. That should be cheap since we compute components anyway when debugging. Toggle via sampling to avoid telemetry explosion.

Lina: Rollout plan? Changing scoring shape is risky for SLA-sensitive tenants.

Alex: Canary rollout flow: 1) smoke tests in staging, 2) deploy scorer as opt-in for a small percentage of requests (tenant+route level), 3) validate cost/latency/regression via Redwood Console evals and traffic tests, 4) scale to 100% with a fast kill switch. We'll expose `policy_rollout` admin API: `curl -X POST /admin/policies/rollout -d '{"policy_id":"pc-2026","ratio":0.1}'`

Chris: Add automated evaluation gates: if p99 latency increases >5ms or cost/unit >3% rollback. Keep these configurable per-tenant.

Priya: Also need a migration path for existing cached decisions: add a background job that rewrites caches for hot tenants to new score_v to reduce cold-start thrash.

Alex: Good idea. Background cache-populate job + warming via traffic replay.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: New policy bundle pc-2026 (matcher_v4, scorer_v3) uploaded by @Alex.

Lina: Security question — scorers will read more signals. Ensure no sensitive tenant fields leak into score_breakdown or logs. We'll redact fields by default.

Mateo: Action items: (1) implement bundle loader with contract validation (Alex), (2) design cache key migration tool (Priya), (3) scorer DSL proto + metrics schema (Lina), (4) canary/rollout admin API + gates (Chris). I'll coordinate the eval dashboards.

Alex: I'll draft a short RFC appendix with the compatibility-checker algorithm and example bundle format. Posting by EOD. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Priya: Ack. Will prepare the cache migration spec and surface perf numbers.

Chris: I'll prototype the gate checks and add them to the canary job.

Lina: I'll write the metric names and redaction rules.

Mateo: Scheduling follow-up sync for next Tue 10am PT.

Alex: Great, meeting invite incoming.
